proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(I_{ia}=\mathbf 1(Z_i=a)\).  By \(\texttt{ass:balanced-complete-randomization}\), for distinct units \(i\ne j\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Z I_{ia}=\frac nN,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_Z(I_{ia}I_{ja})=\frac{n(n-1)}{N(N-1)},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_Z(I_{ia}I_{jb})=\frac{n^2}{N(N-1)}\quad(a\ne b),
\]
whereas \(I_{ia}I_{ib}=0\) when \(a\ne b\).  Define the fixed centered outcomes
\(\widetilde Y_i(a)=Y_i(a)-\bar Y(a)\).  Then
\(\sum_i\widetilde Y_i(a)=0\), and subtracting the fixed mean does not change any assignment covariance.  The preceding inclusion probabilities, together with
\(\sum_{i\ne j}\widetilde Y_i(a)\widetilde Y_j(b)=-\sum_i\widetilde Y_i(a)\widetilde Y_i(b)\), give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a)\mid Y\}
 =\left(\frac1n-\frac1N\right)S_{aa}(Y)
\]
and, for \(a\ne b\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a),\widehat{\bar Y}(b)\mid Y\}
 =-\frac1N S_{ab}(Y).
\]
For example, the latter equality follows equation by equation from
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cov}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(a),\widehat{\bar Y}(b)\mid Y\}
 &=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{Cov}_Z(I_{ia},I_{jb})
       \widetilde Y_i(a)\widetilde Y_j(b)\\
 &=-\frac1{N^2}\sum_i\widetilde Y_i(a)\widetilde Y_i(b)
   +\frac1{N^2(N-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\widetilde Y_i(a)\widetilde Y_j(b)\\
 &=-\frac1{N(N-1)}\sum_i\widetilde Y_i(a)\widetilde Y_i(b)
 =-\frac1N S_{ab}(Y).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus the covariance matrix of \(\widehat{\bar Y}\) is
\(\operatorname{diag}(S_{aa}/n)-S/N\).  Applying the fixed linear map \(C\), as in \(\texttt{def:contrast-risk}\), proves
\[
 \Sigma_C(Y)=C\left\{\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{S_{aa}(Y)}n\right)_{a\in\mathcal A}-\frac{S(Y)}N\right\}C^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Finally, cyclicity of trace and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) yield
\[
 \rho_W(Y)=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[H\left\{\operatorname{diag}(S_{aa}/n)-S/N\right\}\right]
 =\sum_a\frac{H_{aa}S_{aa}(Y)}n-\frac1N\sum_{a,b}H_{ab}S_{ab}(Y).
\]
Holding every armwise empirical multiset fixed holds its mean and its finite-population variance \(S_{aa}(Y)\) fixed by their displayed formulas.  Therefore only the off-diagonal covariances can vary across completions.

First note that \(H\succeq0\) because \(W\succeq0\), and
\(H\mathbf 1_K=C^{\mathsf T}WC\mathbf 1_K=0\) by \(\texttt{ass:causal-contrast}\).  Consequently, in view of \(\texttt{def:rank-cone}\), the only additional requirement for \(H\in\mathcal R_K\) is \(H_{ab}\leq0\) for all \(a\ne b\).

We first prove the needed finite rearrangement fact directly.  Let
\(u_1\leq\cdots\leq u_N\) and \(v_1\leq\cdots\leq v_N\).  If a permutation \(q\) has an inversion at positions \(i<j\), so that \(v_{q(i)}>v_{q(j)}\), swapping those two assigned values changes the sum \(\sum_k u_kv_{q(k)}\) by
\[
 (u_j-u_i)\{v_{q(i)}-v_{q(j)}\}\geq0.
\]
Successively removing inversions therefore proves
\[
 \sum_i u_i v_i\geq\sum_i u_i v_{q(i)}.
\]
Subtracting the fixed product \(N\bar u\bar v\) and dividing by \(N-1>0\) shows that, among all pairings of two fixed empirical marginals, their finite-population covariance is maximized by their common increasing ranks.

Suppose now that \(H\in\mathcal R_K\).  By \(\texttt{def:completion-class}\), every column of a feasible \(Y\) is a permutation of its ordered marginal column in \(Y^{\uparrow}(F)\).  The rearrangement calculation therefore gives, simultaneously for every pair \(a<b\),
\[
 S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}\geq S_{ab}(Y).
\]
The diagonal terms in \(\texttt{lem:complete-randomization-risk}\) are fixed by the marginals, while symmetry of \(H\) and \(S\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)
 &=\frac{2}{N}\sum_{a<b}(-H_{ab})
 \left[S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-S_{ab}(Y)\right]\\
 &\geq0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves sufficiency and the stated regret identity.

Conversely, suppose \(H_{ab}>0\) for some \(a<b\).  Let \(N\) be any multiple of \(2K\), let the marginals in arms \(a,b\) each have \(N/2\) zeros and \(N/2\) ones, and let all other arm marginals be point masses at zero.  Write \(u\) for the ordered binary column.  Common ranking pairs \(u\) with itself, whereas the feasible competing completion pairs arm \(a\)'s column \(u\) with arm \(b\)'s column \(\mathbf 1_N-u\).  The two relevant covariances are
\[
 S_{ab}\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}=\frac{N}{4(N-1)},
 \qquad
 S_{ab}(Y)=-\frac{N}{4(N-1)}.
\]
All marginal variances and all other cross-arm covariances agree between the two schedules.  Hence the already proved identity gives
\[
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)
 =\frac2N(-H_{ab})\frac{N}{2(N-1)}
 =-\frac{H_{ab}}{N-1}<0.
\]
Thus universal common-rank optimality fails whenever an off-diagonal entry of \(H\) is positive.  Together with the automatic positive semidefiniteness and zero row sums established in the first paragraph, this proves necessity and the equivalence.

For a fixed completion pair, a symmetric matrix difference is positive semidefinite exactly when all its quadratic forms are nonnegative.  Thus the asserted universal Loewner dominance is equivalent to
\[
 h^{\mathsf T}\!\left[\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\Sigma_C(Y)\right]h\geq0
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\mathbb R^m,F,Y.
\]
For a given \(h\), put \(c=C^{\mathsf T}h\).  The displayed quadratic form is the scalarized covariance difference for the one-row contrast \(c^{\mathsf T}\) and scalar weight one.  Since \(c^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_K=h^{\mathsf T}C\mathbf 1_K=0\), \(\texttt{thm:rank-cone-iff}\) applies and says that this scalar inequality holds universally exactly when
\[
 cc^{\mathsf T}\in\mathcal R_K,
 \quad\text{equivalently}\quad
 c_ac_b\leq0\quad(a\ne b).
\]
Therefore universal Loewner dominance is equivalent to the following property of the linear space \(L=\operatorname{range}(C^{\mathsf T})\): every \(c\in L\) has pairwise nonpositive distinct-coordinate products.

We now characterize such a space.  Every nonzero \(c\in L\) has coordinate sum zero.  It therefore has a positive and a negative coordinate.  Pairwise nonpositive products prohibit two positive coordinates and also prohibit two negative coordinates.  Hence every nonzero \(c\in L\) has exactly two nonzero coordinates and is of the form \(t(e_p-e_q)\).  Fix one such vector.  If another vector in \(L\) used a different coordinate pair, then a generic nonzero linear combination of the two vectors (choose the scalar outside the finitely many values causing coordinate cancellation) would have at least three nonzero coordinates, contradicting the preceding conclusion.  It follows that
\[
 L\subseteq\operatorname{span}(e_p-e_q)
\]
for one fixed pair \(p\ne q\).  Equivalently, all columns of \(C\) except columns \(p,q\) vanish and \(C_{\cdot q}=-C_{\cdot p}\).  Because \(C\ne0\), this is a nonzero vector rescaling of the pairwise contrast.  Conversely, this column form makes every \(C^{\mathsf T}h\) a multiple of \(e_p-e_q\), so every matrix \(cc^{\mathsf T}\) lies in \(\mathcal R_K\), proving Loewner dominance.

If \(C\) does not have this form, the characterization supplies an \(h\) and distinct arms \(a,b\) with \(c_ac_b>0\).  The binary construction in the necessity part of \(\texttt{thm:rank-cone-iff}\), applied to \(cc^{\mathsf T}\), then gives
\[
 h^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}h
 <h^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_C(Y)h.
\]
This is precisely the claimed binary witness that common ranking reduces the randomization variance in direction \(h\).

Under the stated values,
\[
 H=C^{\mathsf T}WC=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}\in\mathcal R_2.
\]
Hence \(\texttt{thm:rank-cone-iff}\) proves that common ranks maximize \(\rho_W\).  Under the stated scalar choices, \(\rho_W(Y)\) is exactly
\(\operatorname{Var}_Z\{\widehat{\bar Y}(2)-\widehat{\bar Y}(1)\mid Y\}\).  The maximum is sharp because \(Y^{\uparrow}(F)\) belongs to the completion class and attains it, and it is comonotone because it pairs the two marginal order-statistic columns in their common increasing order.  This is exactly the two-arm endpoint named in the proposition.

With \(W=I_{K-1}\), one has \(H=C^{\mathsf T}C\).  Because the rows of \(C\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\mathbf 1_K^{\perp}\), \(C^{\mathsf T}C\) is the orthogonal projector onto that space.  The projector is
\[
 H=I_K-\frac1K\mathbf 1_K\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Consequently \(H_{aa}=1-K^{-1}\), \(H_{ab}=-K^{-1}\) for \(a\ne b\), \(H\succeq0\), and \(H\mathbf 1_K=0\).  By \(\texttt{def:rank-cone}\), \(H\in\mathcal R_K\), so \(\texttt{thm:rank-cone-iff}\) proves that common ranks maximize the sum of the component randomization variances.  If \(K>2\), this \(C\) has rank \(K-1>1\), whereas a matrix supported on two opposite columns has rank at most one.  The characterization in \(\texttt{thm:loewner-boundary}\) therefore rules out universal Loewner dominance, as claimed.

Direct multiplication gives
\[
 C^{\mathsf T}C=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-1&0\\-1&2&-1\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}=H.
\]
This matrix is positive semidefinite as a Gram matrix, has zero row sums, and has nonpositive off-diagonal entries; hence \(H\in\mathcal R_3\) by \(\texttt{def:rank-cone}\).  For the common binary column, the mean is \(1/2\) and
\[
 \frac1{N-1}\sum_{i=1}^N(Y_i-1/2)^2
 =\frac15\cdot6\cdot\frac14=\frac3{10}.
\]
Thus every entry of the common-rank covariance matrix is \(3/10\).  In the competing schedule, the second centered column is the negative of the first and third centered columns, proving
\(S_{12}=S_{23}=-3/10\) and \(S_{13}=3/10\).

For the common schedule, \(\sum_{a,b}H_{ab}S_{ab}=(3/10)\mathbf 1_3^{\mathsf T}H\mathbf 1_3=0\), while
\(\sum_a H_{aa}S_{aa}/n=(1+2+1)(3/10)/2=3/5\).  Therefore \(\texttt{lem:complete-randomization-risk}\) gives \(\rho_W=3/5\).  For the competing schedule,
\[
 \sum_{a,b}H_{ab}S_{ab}
 =\frac65+2\left\{(-1)\left(-\frac3{10}\right)+(-1)\left(-\frac3{10}\right)\right\}
 =\frac{12}{5},
\]
so its risk is \(3/5-(1/6)(12/5)=1/5\).  Finally the regret identity in \(\texttt{thm:rank-cone-iff}\) yields
\[
 \frac13\left\{\frac3{10}-\left(-\frac3{10}\right)+\frac3{10}-\left(-\frac3{10}\right)\right\}=\frac25,
\]
which also equals \(3/5-1/5\).

The stated matrix is the outer product
\[
 H=(1,1,-2)^{\mathsf T}(1,1,-2)
 =\begin{pmatrix}1&1&-2\\1&1&-2\\-2&-2&4\end{pmatrix}.
\]
It is positive semidefinite and has zero row sums, but \(H_{12}=1>0\), so \(H\notin\mathcal R_3\) by \(\texttt{def:rank-cone}\).  Each nonconstant binary column has mean \(1/2\) and variance \((5^{-1})6(1/4)=3/10\); the third column is constant.  Under common ranking, \(S_{12}=3/10\).  Thus \(\texttt{lem:complete-randomization-risk}\) gives
\[
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}
 =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac3{10}+\frac3{10}\right)
 -\frac16\left\{\frac3{10}+\frac3{10}+2\frac3{10}\right\}
 =\frac1{10}.
\]
After reversing only the second column, its centered values are the negatives of those in the first, so \(S_{12}=-3/10\).  The same formula then gives
\[
 \rho_W(Y)
 =\frac3{10}-\frac16\left\{\frac3{10}+\frac3{10}-2\frac3{10}\right\}
 =\frac3{10}.
\]
Equivalently, the exact regret identity gives
\[
 \rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)
 =\frac13(-1)\left\{\frac3{10}-\left(-\frac3{10}\right)\right\}
 =-\frac15.
\]
The reversed schedule preserves both nondegenerate empirical marginals and the degenerate third marginal, so it is a valid member of \(\mathcal S_6(F)\) and is the required strict finite witness.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) and let \(E=\mathcal A\times\{1,\ldots,N-1\}\).  For \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) and \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\), define the symmetric \(|E|\times|E|\) matrix \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\), indexed by \((a,r),(b,s)\in E\), by
\[
 B^{\pi,\sigma}_{(a,r),(b,s)}
 =H_{ab}\sum_{i,j=1}^N\Omega_{ab,\pi(i),\pi(j)}
 \left[(d_r)_i(d_s)_j-(d_r)_{\sigma_a(i)}(d_s)_{\sigma_b(j)}\right].
\]
Then
\[
 [\Omega]_{\cong}\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{there is a \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) such that every \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is copositive},
\]
where copositive means \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}\alpha\geq0\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^{K(N-1)}\).  This equivalence gives an exact finite recognition algorithm.  Enumerate \(\pi\) and \(\sigma\).  For each nonempty principal support \(T\subseteq E\) and each negative real algebraic eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(B^{\pi,\sigma}_{TT}\), test by exact linear feasibility whether
\[
 \bigl(B^{\pi,\sigma}_{TT}-\lambda I\bigr)v=0,
 \qquad v_t\geq1\quad(t\in T).
\]
The matrix \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is copositive exactly when every one of these systems is infeasible.  If \(H\) and \(\Omega\) are rational, a yes instance returns a relabelling \(\pi\), exact isolating data for the negative algebraic eigenvalues, and, for every associated eigenspace, an exact linear-infeasibility certificate for intersection with the strict positive orthant.  A no instance returns, for every common relabelling \(\pi\), an arm-specific permutation \(\sigma\) and rational nonnegative cut increments \(\alpha\) for which the loss improvement is strict.

For a no instance, define
\[
 L^*(H,\Omega)=
 \max_{\pi\in\mathfrak S_N}
 \min_{\substack{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K,\ \alpha\geq0\\
 \alpha^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}\alpha<0}}
 \max_{a\in\mathcal A}\left(1+\#\{r:\alpha_{(a,r)}>0\}\right).
\]
Then \(L^*(H,\Omega)\) is exactly the smallest per-arm alphabet size sufficient for a complete family of strict witnesses against all common relabellings.  In particular \(L^*(H,\Omega)\leq N\), and binary witnesses are complete for the given no instance exactly when \(L^*(H,\Omega)\leq2\).  The exhaustive algorithm is finite but generally exponential in \(N\) and \(K\); this partial theorem does not establish the polynomial running-time requested in \(\texttt{oeq:general-balanced-kernel}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\pi\) and abbreviate \(\widetilde\Omega=\Omega^\pi\).  By \(\texttt{def:admissible-balanced-kernel}\),
\[
 \sum_i\widetilde\Omega_{abij}=0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \sum_j\widetilde\Omega_{abij}=0
\]
for every choice of the remaining indices.  Every ordered column has the unique adjacent-increment expansion from \(\texttt{def:kernel-cut-handle}\),
\[
 x^a=x^a_1\mathbf 1_N+\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\alpha_{(a,r)}d_r,
 \qquad
 \alpha_{(a,r)}=x^a_{r+1}-x^a_r\geq0.
\]
The two unit-sum identities annihilate every term involving a constant column.  Substitution into \(\texttt{def:balanced-kernel-loss}\) therefore gives the exact identity
\[
 N^2\left\{\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})-
 \mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)\right\}
 =\alpha^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}\alpha.
\]
The covariance symmetry \(\Omega_{abij}=\Omega_{baji}\) and symmetry of \(H\) show, after interchanging \((a,r,i)\) with \((b,s,j)\), that \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) is symmetric.  Since every \(\alpha\geq0\) produces ordered columns through the displayed expansion, and every ordered column produces such an \(\alpha\), the identity proves
\[
 \Omega^\pi\in\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 B^{\pi,\sigma}\text{ is copositive for every }\sigma.
\]
Taking the existential quantifier over \(\pi\) and applying \(\texttt{def:admissible-rank-kernel-domain}\) proves the first asserted equivalence.

It remains to justify that the test and certificates are finite.  For any real symmetric \(q\times q\) matrix \(B\), the following elementary support criterion holds:
\[
 B\text{ is not copositive}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{some nonempty principal submatrix \(B_{TT}\) has a negative eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector}.
\]
The reverse implication is immediate by extending the positive eigenvector by zeros.  For the forward implication, minimize \(v^{\mathsf T}Bv\) on the compact set \(\{v\geq0:\|v\|_2=1\}\).  If \(B\) is not copositive, the minimum \(\lambda\) is negative.  On the support \(T\) of a minimizer, all coordinates are strictly positive, so the Lagrange multiplier equation in the relative interior of that coordinate face is
\(B_{TT}v_T=\lambda v_T\).  Multiplication by \(v_T^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\|v_T\|_2=1\) show that the multiplier is exactly \(\lambda=v^{\mathsf T}Bv<0\).  This proves the criterion.

There are only \(2^q-1\) nonempty supports.  For a fixed support and negative eigenvalue \(\lambda\), the eigenspace meets the strict positive orthant if and only if it contains a vector whose coordinates are all at least one: the forward implication follows by positive rescaling by the reciprocal of the smallest coordinate, and the reverse implication is immediate.  Thus the intersection test is exactly the linear feasibility problem
\[
 (B_{TT}-\lambda I)v=0,\qquad v_t\geq1\quad(t\in T),
\]
not merely a spectral-sign test.  When \(B\) is rational, its eigenvalues are real algebraic.  Characteristic-polynomial root isolation gives exact ordered-field representations of those eigenvalues; exact row reduction followed by Fourier--Motzkin elimination decides each displayed system and supplies a finite elimination certificate of feasibility or infeasibility.  Combining these finitely many tests with the finite sets \(\mathfrak S_N\) and \(\mathfrak S_N^K\) proves termination and the asserted yes certificate.

On a failing support, take the strictly positive algebraic eigenvector and extend it by zero.  The inequalities defining positivity on its support and \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}B\alpha<0\) are strict and hence persist on an open neighborhood in that coordinate face.  Density of the rationals therefore supplies a rational \(\alpha\geq0\) with the same strict quadratic inequality; exact rational interval refinement constructs one.  For this rational vector, set
\[
 x^a=\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\alpha_{(a,r)}d_r.
\]
The loss identity proves that \(\sigma\) strictly improves on identity.  This arm column has exactly one plus the number of its positive adjacent increments as its number of distinct values.  Minimizing this discrete count over all strict witnesses for a fixed \(\pi\), and then taking the maximum over the relabellings that all must be refuted, proves the formula for \(L^*(H,\Omega)\).  Each arm has at most \(N-1\) positive increments, so \(L^*(H,\Omega)\leq N\); the value is at most two exactly when one cut per nonconstant arm suffices.  The displayed enumeration has factorial and exponential components, so it proves exact decidability and certificate production, but not a polynomial running-time bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Whether membership in the admissible label-free cone can be recognized in time polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and the rational input bit length while returning the requested exact yes or no certificate; absent such an algorithm, a faithful hardness or impossibility theorem for this feasible balanced-kernel domain is also not yet proved.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact copositivity characterization requires, in the direct algorithm, enumeration of \(N!\) common relabellings, \(N!^K\) arm-specific permutations, and up to \(2^{K(N-1)}-1\) principal supports for each cut-product matrix. General copositivity complexity does not by itself settle the restricted moment-polytope image \(\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), so no unrestricted hardness claim transfers without a new reduction that preserves balanced-law feasibility.
open_obligations.attempted: Expanded every ordered column into adjacent cut increments, reduced universal identity-optimality exactly to copositivity of explicit matrices \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\), and made each support test exact by intersecting every negative algebraic eigenspace with the strict positive orthant through linear feasibility. This gives terminating factorial/exponential recognition and exact certificates, but neither compresses the permutation search nor yields a feasibility-preserving hardness reduction.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved partial result \(\texttt{thm:general-balanced-kernel-copositive-characterization}\) converts the universal ordered-column comparison into finitely many copositivity tests on explicit cut-product matrices \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\).  Copositivity is decided exactly by enumerating principal supports and, for every negative algebraic eigenvalue, testing its eigenspace for intersection with the strict positive orthant through exact linear feasibility.  It returns exact yes certificates, rational strict no witnesses, and the exact minimal per-arm alphabet number \(L^*(H,\Omega)\leq N\).  Its enumeration is factorial/exponential and therefore does not supply the polynomial-time recognition algorithm demanded by the open-ended question.

prose_updates.tldr: Under balanced complete randomization, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if the contrast Gram matrix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. This gives an \(O(K^2)\) certificate, exact six-unit checks, and a binary counterexample outside the cone. Universal Loewner dominance is possible only for a rescaled single pairwise contrast. For arbitrary admissible balanced assignment kernels, an explicit finite cut-product construction now characterizes rank preservation by copositivity and yields exact algebraic certificates and a minimal witness alphabet; polynomial-time recognition remains open.

project_justification.gap: Sharp rank completion is analytic for the two-arm difference-in-means estimator, whereas generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion remains universally least favourable in a multi-arm experiment, nor an exact label-invariant cut characterization restricted to realizable nonexchangeable balanced covariance kernels. The complexity of recognizing that latter feasible-domain cone also remains unsettled.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for complete randomization, a stronger classification for joint covariance dominance, and a finite copositivity characterization over the exact balanced-law moment polytope modulo common unit relabelling. The finite characterization is exact but is not claimed to be polynomial-time.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete-randomization risk decomposition, proves the graph-Laplacian iff theorem by pairwise rearrangement and isolated binary necessity witnesses, evaluates both mechanisms exactly at \(K=3,N=6\), and classifies the Loewner case. For general balanced kernels it expands ordered columns in cut generators, proves an exact copositivity characterization, gives algebraic yes certificates and rational strict no witnesses, and characterizes the minimal per-arm witness alphabet, while isolating polynomial-time recognition as the remaining open obligation.

prose_updates.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee establish the two-arm comonotone sharp endpoint; Proposition 4 recovers that result exactly. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion to obtain a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply the arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance identity used in Lemma 1 but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem covers the classical pairwise rearrangement ingredient, while the proof here gives the required finite swap argument directly. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming. The balanced-kernel extension instead restricts coefficients to the exact finite moment-polytope image of fixed-count, marginally balanced laws and proves a finite copositivity characterization modulo common relabelling. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz quadratic-assignment theorem motivates the cut decomposition but does not provide necessity, feasible-kernel recognition, or the still-open polynomial-time algorithm claimed here only as an open question.
prose_updates.interpretation: For complete randomization, checking whether one common-rank completion is least favourable for a prespecified scalar loss requires only checking the off-diagonal signs of \(H\). Joint covariance dominance is much narrower and survives only on one pairwise-contrast ray. Under a nonexchangeable balanced law, rank preservation is still exactly decidable from the design covariance tensor: cut increments turn every possible ordered marginal schedule into a nonnegative vector, and identity-optimality becomes copositivity of finitely many explicit matrices. The current certificate is exact rather than computationally efficient in the worst case.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate concerns a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\); it does not turn that scalar endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion dominates every linear combination. For a general admissible balanced kernel, the proved recognition procedure enumerates relabellings, arm permutations, supports, and algebraic eigenspace feasibility problems and is therefore factorial/exponential; no polynomial-time algorithm or feasible-domain hardness theorem is established. Binary failure witnesses are complete only when the proved quantity \(L^*(H,\Omega)\) is at most two.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The complete-randomization cone theorem follows from the design covariance identity, a finite rearrangement argument, and a new necessity classification; its novelty is the causal contrast geometry and Loewner boundary, not a new general dependence inequality. The \(K=3,N=6\) propositions are exact audit certificates rather than asymptotic claims. On the exact covariance-tensor image of fixed-count, marginally balanced assignment laws, the general extension is proved only to the level of a finite copositivity characterization, exact algebraic yes certificates, rational strict no witnesses, and the minimal finite witness alphabet. The explicit polynomial-time recognition requirement remains open. The project does not claim finite-sample tail dominance, empirical-marginal inference, or a closed form outside the certified complete-randomization cone.

statement_notes.justification: The feasible moment-polytope domain makes universal rank preservation a label-invariant design question; the exact finite characterization now isolates computational complexity rather than algebraic decidability as the remaining issue.
statement_notes.gap: The cut-product copositivity theorem yields a terminating exact algorithm, but it enumerates relabellings, permutations, and supports. Neither a polynomial-time recognition algorithm nor a hardness theorem respecting the balanced-law covariance image has been proved.
statement_notes.consumer: A future design tool needs either a polynomial compression of the exact certificate or a principled complexity barrier before the general nonexchangeable rule can replace exhaustive completion search at scale.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem gives a computable side of the general-kernel problem: a necessary-and-sufficient finite copositivity test with exact yes certificates, rational strict no witnesses, and an exact minimal witness alphabet.
statement_notes.gap: Existing transport and quadratic-assignment formulations do not specialize universal rank preservation to the exact balanced assignment-law covariance polytope with label invariance and finite cut certificates.
statement_notes.consumer: Design analysts can exactly audit a fixed rational balanced kernel and recover a concrete failing completion when common ranks are not identity-optimal, while recognizing that the direct procedure is exponential.
